title: Return an empty list, never null

blocks.text: A method that returns a collection returns an empty one when it has nothing to give, never `null`, so its callers can loop over the result without a null check.
Write `first(int count)` in `EvenNumbers`. It returns a new, modifiable list of the first `count` even numbers, starting from `0`:

items: every call returns a list of its own: a caller may add to it.

cases.says: first(0) and first(-5) are empty lists, not null.
The list from first(0) can be added to, and a caller's change reaches no other call.

concepts: A method that returns a collection returns an empty one, never null.
